title: a statically imported foreign module without a leading @module/@throws {never} initialization claim is rejected
notes: The untrusted module's call also loses its Result, so both reports belong to the contract. 2026-08-25: the second report is now the subject of an `xfail` (go) rather than a rewritten expectation. The ownership question the marker settles is recorded in full there; the short version is that 09-foreign-calls/the-never-annotation-is-case-sensitive pins the identical SMITHERS1301@4:11 over the identical program shape with a TRUSTED module header and passes on both backends, so the diagnostic is not a cascade of the trust refusal. This case is also the one that caught an attempt to make container literals unconditionally transparent in the reference's must-consume walk: `shout` is LIFTED to `Result<string, Panic>` while its declaration still says `string`, so the array's type is `string[]`, the array does not hold the channel, and the store is a fiction. Do not weaken it. RETIRED 2026-08-25, the `go` marker: the fork's early return that disabled the ENTIRE foreign policy for every call behind a refused module edge was removed, so the SMITHERS1301 for the Result the untrusted call discards is reported again. The suppression was far broader than the one diagnostic it was written for — it also disabled the panic row, SMITHERS1502, SMITHERS1506 and SMITHERS1507 — and enumerating the class found four broken call forms where one had been reported. The async form is now pinned beside this case as 09-foreign-calls/an-async-function-returning-an-untrusted-foreign-result-charges-both. Measured XPASS on both backends before the marker was deleted.
